claim: The guide defines high agency as choosing a worthwhile direction, finding room to influence events, taking appropriate action and learning.

evidence_refs.note: Supplies the popular resourcefulness idea used as one input to the guide's explicitly proposed definition.
Supplies intentional action and reflective regulation used as the other input; does not validate the combined definition.

caveats: Working synthesis, not a standardized psychometric definition.

claim: The 2016 official episode and transcript contain an influential modern formulation of the phrase.

evidence_refs.note: Official page dates the episode January 13, 2016; transcript contains the high agency discussion.

caveats: Not proof of earliest coinage.

claim: Human agency theory includes intentionality, forethought, self regulation and reflection, with social influences and personal, proxy and collective modes.

evidence_refs.note: Abstract expressly lists four agentic functions, three modes, and interaction with social systems.

caveats: Only publisher abstract inspected.

claim: Self efficacy concerns perceived capability for specific actions and outcomes; mastery and examples can inform it, but measurement can mix capability and motivation.

locator.value: The breakthrough; Self-efficacy today; Sources of self-efficacy

evidence_refs.note: Review explains task-specific capability beliefs, mastery and modeling, and the dispute about conflation with motivation.

caveats: Professional synthesis used; original 1977 article not accessed. Measurement critique remains contested.

claim: The Togo randomized initiative training study assigned 1500 entrepreneurs to three arms; profits improved about 30 percent versus control over two years after structured training.

evidence_refs.note: Abstract reports 1500 participants and 30-percent versus 11-percent effects; design describes randomized arms and training intensity.

caveats: Selected established microentrepreneurs; 36-hour training plus follow-up visits; no universal 30-percent benefit. Traditional arm estimate 11 percent nonsignificant.

claim: Long-term follow up reported larger gains for men than women and unresolved mechanisms.

locator.value: Long-term results; Why do we see these gender differences emerging?

evidence_refs.note: Investigator reports divergent long-term gender effects and evaluates mechanisms without settling one cause.

caveats: Investigator's blog account, not independently inspected full follow-up paper. Attrition and subgroup precision matter.

claim: A staggered workplace AI rollout covering 5172 support agents increased issues resolved per hour by about 15 percent on average.

evidence_refs.note: Author version reports 5172 agents and 15-percent issues-per-hour gains; adoption section describes staggered rollout.

caveats: Setting-specific rollout; not a broad randomized test of all work.

claim: The GPT-4 consulting experiment involved 758 participants; tasks inside the frontier improved while one outside task showed a 19-percentage-point correctness decline.

evidence_refs.note: Published results describe the randomized 758-consultant design, inside-frontier gains and outside-task decline expressed in percentage points.

caveats: Published 2026 report describes earlier GPT-4 experiment; 12.2 percent more tasks and 25.1 percent faster inside frontier. Percentage points, not relative percent, for decline.

claim: Standard GPT-4 assistance in a Turkish school math experiment harmed unaided exam performance by 17 percent relative to control; guarded tutoring avoided harm without demonstrated exam improvement.

evidence_refs.note: Paper compares randomized treatments and subsequent unassisted exams, showing base-treatment harm and no demonstrated tutor exam gain.

caveats: Specific classroom systems and subject; cannot generalize to every learner, model or tutoring design.

claim: In a 319-worker survey, higher confidence in AI was associated with less reported critical thinking.

evidence_refs.note: Survey abstract states the sample size and confidence association; limitations restrict interpretation to reported effort and correlation.

caveats: Self-report and correlation, not experimentally demonstrated long-term skill loss.

claim: A February 2026 METR update explains selection bias and measurement problems limiting newer productivity estimates.

locator.value: Selection effects and updated experiment design

evidence_refs.note: Investigators describe selection and measurement problems that undermine precise interpretation of their newer estimates.

caveats: Does not yield a trustworthy universal current estimate.

claim: AI assistance can expand feasible actions, increasing the practical importance of goal selection and checking outcomes.

evidence_refs.note: Productivity gains support feasibility of expanded assistance in some tasks, not a measured agency interaction.
Heterogeneous task results motivate checking tool fitness and accuracy.
Divergence between supported practice and unaided learning motivates preserving human judgment.

caveats: Interpretation; evidence does not test high agency as moderator or prove job-displacement immunity.

claim: The MCII meta-analysis includes 21 studies and finds small-to-moderate average improvements with heterogeneity and possible publication bias.

evidence_refs.note: Meta-analysis reports 21 studies, positive average effects, heterogeneity and possible publication bias.

caveats: 24 independent effects, N15907, g=.336; adjusted estimate lower; not universal nor a 14-day programme.

claim: The progress monitoring meta-analysis covers 138 randomized studies and 19951 participants, with positive average goal attainment effects.

evidence_refs.note: Experimental synthesis reports 138 studies and 19951 participants; moderator comparisons concern recording and reporting.

caveats: d=.40; recording/reporting moderator differences do not alone demonstrate mechanism causality.

claim: Psychological safety was associated with learning behavior in a study of 51 manufacturing teams.

evidence_refs.note: Paper reports 51-team observational sample and the association between psychological safety and learning behavior.

caveats: Observational mixed methods, not a randomized safety intervention.

claim: The phrase is visible in 2026 technology hiring discussion, but evidence here does not quantify broad popularity or growth.

locator.value: Reported interviews about agency and hiring

evidence_refs.note: Reported interviews explicitly discuss agency in hiring; no population or search-volume series is provided.

caveats: One community and reporting sample; no search-volume series collected.

claim: The four-step action loop and two-week practice plan are original evidence-informed suggestions.

evidence_refs.note: Intentionality, regulation and reflection inform the proposed loop.
Obstacle planning informs one practice step, not the complete proposed schedule.
Progress monitoring informs the feedback step, not a validation of the full plan.

caveats: No direct validation of this combination, schedule, informal questions or illustrative AI prompt.

claim: AI assistance always improves performance and understanding.

evidence_refs.note: Task correctness declined with AI.
Unassisted exam performance declined in the base treatment.

caveats: Challenge hypothesis rejected; removed as a possible universal conclusion.

claim: Hall's essay recommends making requests and seeking feedback; it is practitioner advice.

evidence_refs.note: Essay directly recommends feedback and requests; article is a firsthand advice essay rather than an experimental evaluation.

caveats: Not evidence of causal efficacy or a validated training programme.

claim: A proposed division of work has a person choose the goal, AI assist with options and drafting, and real feedback guide revision.

evidence_refs.note: Provides evidence that AI assistance can support concrete work in an appropriate setting.
Motivates choosing suitable uses and checking actual correctness, rather than trusting surface polish.
Motivates distinguishing assisted output from human learning and using appropriate feedback.

caveats: Illustrative workshop scenario, not a tested allocation protocol or a report of an event that occurred.
Roles are recommendations, not exclusive capabilities or a guaranteed benefit.

claim: The published P&G experiment analyzed 791 professionals; individuals with AI produced solutions comparable in quality to two-person teams without AI, and AI-assisted proposals balanced commercial and technical perspectives across professional backgrounds.

evidence_refs.note: Randomized four-condition design, AI-plus-training package, quality and expertise results. Endnote distinguishes 791 completers from 776 complete surveys.

caveats: One company, one-day remote product-development workshop, GPT-4 with training; not proof that an individual can replace an ongoing team.

claim: In the P&G experiment, AI improved generated idea quality without improving selection of the best idea from the generated portfolio.

evidence_refs.note: AI increased idea quality, while selection accuracy did not improve; selected outcomes still improved due to stronger starting material.

caveats: Five initial ideas per portfolio by design. Selection pattern does not establish a general psychological mechanism or a universal AI effect.

claim: High agency can be understood as an AI-era superpower in the practical sense of using expanded assistance to begin feasible work, contribute across skills, test ideas sooner and exercise judgment.

evidence_refs.note: Supports assistance gains and reduced barriers in a particular workplace.
Supports expanded reach and distinguishes idea generation from selection.
Provides benefits and countervailing correctness failure, motivating judgment.
Supports seeking and using feedback; not the complete proposed AI workflow.

caveats: Superpower is an explanatory metaphor, not a validated high-agency trait effect.
No cited study tests whether high-agency people uniquely benefit from AI.
Faster testing is a proposed opportunity conditional on reduced preparation time and actual external feedback, not a measured compounding growth rate.

claim: The revised AI diagram proposes that expanded AI options become useful through human goal selection, checked action and real feedback.

evidence_refs.note: Supports AI assistance for concrete tasks.
Supports wider possibilities alongside selection limits.
Motivates checking actual work against its intended goal.

caveats: Original explanatory synthesis, not a tested causal model, fixed division of capability or guaranteed result.

claim: Self-determination theory distinguishes autonomous and controlled motivation, includes personally endorsed instrumental action, and does not equate autonomy with independence or individualism.

evidence_refs.note: The inspected passage directly establishes this bounded assertion.

caveats: Theory and research review; not a validated high-agency intervention or an individual diagnosis.

claim: Three cross-sectional studies found associations between goal disengagement/reengagement capacities and aspects of well-being, without establishing causality.

evidence_refs.note: The inspected passage directly establishes this bounded assertion.

caveats: Self-report associations; direction of causation unresolved; not proof that quitting always improves well-being.

claim: The Togo trial randomized 1,500 existing small business owners to three groups of 500; initiative training included opportunities, goals, planning, feedback and overcoming obstacles, with classes and follow up visits.

evidence_refs.note: Directly inspected curriculum and three-group assignment.

caveats: Selected established nonfarm microenterprise owners; training package, not a slogan or the proposed two week exercise.

claim: The mathematics study compared base, guarded tutor and no-AI conditions; the tutor used teacher-prepared solutions, mistakes and hints with instructions not to reveal the entire answer. The reported exam contrast concerned immediate unaided performance.

evidence_refs.note: Directly inspected safeguards and short-term performance boundary.

caveats: Specific historical GPT-4 interfaces and one Turkish high school; safeguards are not proved universally effective and no long-term retention result is claimed.

claim: Version 2 supplies the definitions, study comparisons, causal and statistical limitations, examples and media guidance needed to explain the declared high agency topic without external retrieval. References are optional verification and attribution.

evidence_refs.note: Relevant intervention context is explained inline.
Guardrails and immediate unaided outcome are explained inline.
Motivation concepts are defined inline.

caveats: Self-contained within the declared narrative and media scope, not exhaustive coverage of every source or an answer to unresolved empirical questions.
Filled practice record and source-only exercise are original unvalidated teaching examples.
